subtasks: S1 action-protocol: ActionCapability.PUBLISH + publish payload + key-level three-state serializer + not-wired 501
S2 policy-engine: deterministic fail-closed verdict between plan_action and resolve_action
S3 action-executor: PUBLISH via Tool Gateway, idempotency key wired, RetryPolicy unlocked

S4a DONE: run_publish submits through the Tool Gateway (no more self-built XHSClient); xhs.publish orphan disappears; cdp_endpoint joins the tool signature so per-account profiles survive the migration; account_id finally reaches the platform layer on the mainline path (closing the other half of the S2 defect)

S4b DONE (feat/p2a-s4b-publish-confirmation): publish_gate between the AI verdict and the irreversible publish; dynamic interrupt + Command(resume=...); WorkflowStatus.AWAITING_PUBLISH wired into BOTH derive_status paths; auto_publish honoured (it was declared-but-unread) so the default path is unchanged; separate publish_confirmation key (never human_feedback); default-refuse on any value that is not the literal 'confirmed'; /resume has NO default decision. Does NOT emit a PublishIntent, so open question 1 stays open -- see the revision note in prd.md.
notes:
S4b landed on feat/p2a-s4b-publish-confirmation (base ce9eff54). Scope: only the WAIT. A human authorisation gate (`publish_gate`) now sits between the AI quality verdict and the irreversible publish -- until this slice 'the content is good enough' and 'you may post it' were the SAME event, so an AI gate could decide on its own to perform an irreversible external action. The gate uses a DYNAMIC interrupt() (not interrupt_before) for two reasons, neither stylistic: Command(resume=...) only resumes dynamic interrupts (brief/ripple/blogger already use that channel; a static entry would need a second one just for this gate), and builder.compile() appears TWICE in build_graph() (dev/prod) so interrupt_before would put 'this gate exists' in two places while add_node writes it once -- single entry, no drift. SIX pre-existing facts had to be handled first: (1) two interrupt paradigms coexist in this repo; (2) WorkflowStatus is DERIVED, not stored, and derive_status recognises a gate through TWO independent paths (next_nodes gate name, and interrupts[0].value['gate']) -- both were extended, since adding one leaves the other silently misreporting; (3) `auto_publish` was a DECLARED-BUT-UNREAD key: POST /start and POST /api/review/submit both advertise '审核通过后自动发布', the schema/DB/state all carry it, and backend/graph/** never read it -- this slice honours it, which is precisely what keeps the change to the DEFAULT path only (without it, every existing auto-publish workflow would suddenly need a human click -- that is changing behaviour, not adding a gate); (4) `dry_run` has two sources (workflow-level state + decision-level publish_options) and its rule lived inline in PublisherAgent.execute; (5) run_publish has THREE call sites and the other two (/publish-retry, the free-publish route) are ALREADY explicit human channels, so no gate was added there; (6) 'cancelled' is not new semantics -- derive_status priority 1 and _check_terminal already map phase=CANCELLED, so refusing a publish needs NO new status value, only AWAITING_PUBLISH. KEY DESIGN: (a) publish_confirmation is a SEPARATE state key from human_feedback -- merging the two is the natural refactor and it would silently break routing, because review_outcome reads human_feedback.decision, so a gate write there would overwrite the verdict it routes on; (b) the failure direction is CLOSED: publish_gate_outcome only accepts the literal 'confirmed', everything else (missing, typo, old client) is a refusal, because a confirmation gate that reads an unrecognised value as 'go ahead' turns every version skew into an unconfirmed real publish; (c) there is deliberately NO default resume_value, unlike brief/ripple/blogger whose defaults ('skip'/'accept') continue something already authorised -- here the default would BE the irreversible act, so an empty /resume describes what to send and runs nothing; (d) a refusal sets phase=CANCELLED rather than ERROR (a human saying 'not this one' is a decision, not a fault) and rather than leaving PUBLISHING (publisher is skipped, so the run would have no next node and derive_status would report COMPLETED for a note never posted); (e) publish_is_dry_run is now ONE rule with TWO readers (PublisherAgent picks its mock path, the gate decides whether to ask), so gate and publisher cannot disagree about whether anything left the machine -- which is why auto_publish is compared with strict `is True` (no twin reader: a near-miss value means nobody really made the statement, so stay closed) while dry_run uses truthiness (its twin would also go mock, so they agree). REVISION vs the plan row: the row also promised 'PublisherAgent emits a PublishIntent and stops there' plus a ruling on open question 1. That half was NOT built -- routing the mainline through the control plane (intent -> Policy -> Executor) is an architectural migration, orthogonal to the safety property 'never publish without human authorisation' (the same split argument as S4a), and S4a had already settled on not emitting intents. So the mainline still calls run_publish directly and open question 1 (ActionIntentRequest.account_id required vs the mainline's implicit account) REMAINS UNADJUDICATED -- this slice has no code path that produces an ActionIntent, so there is nothing for the ruling to attach to. Recorded as a revision in prd.md rather than left as a plan row that looks done. GATES: pytest -q 3227 passed / 3 skipped (S4a's 3151 / 3 skipped + 76 = 36 + 9 + 10 + 4 + 1 + 14 + 2, exactly the new cases added -- nothing deleted, no existing assertion weakened); ruff check + ruff format --check clean; mypy backend --python-version 3.12 clean (203 files); P1b baseline drift within threshold; tool_runtime_gate.py OK; frontend type-check + vitest + i18n:check clean. MUTATION CHECK 22/22 killed, each applied from pristine content with a named killer, and all 16 named killers were first run on the untouched tree so no 'killed' verdict can come from an already-red test. Two notable ones: M12's FIRST run was an ANCHOR FAILURE, not a survivor (it anchored on `if terminal := _check_terminal(state)`, a shape 15 routers share) -- the recorded result is the re-run after tightening the anchor. And a probe side-product: Command(resume={}) does NOT resolve the interrupt at all -- LangGraph reads an empty payload as 'nothing to resume with', the node re-raises and the thread stays parked with an untouched state. That is the safest reading of a blank answer and it is distinguishable from a refusal, so it got its own test rather than being folded into the refusal group. TRIPWIRES: the evaluator-gate topology test pinning 'the publisher verdict edge lands on the publisher node' went red by design and was RESHAPED, not deleted (renamed, expectation moved to publish_gate, plus two new assertions for the gate's own branch); tests/integration/test_evaluator_pause_resume.py's next-node assertion moved (("publisher",) -> ("publish_gate",)) under the same discipline as S4a's orphan tripwire.

-- S4a --
S4a landed on feat/p2a-s4a-mainline-gateway (base 5a76cd8a). Scope: only the SUBMIT moved. run_publish no longer builds an XHSClient; it makes one `runtime.tools.invoke("xhs.publish", payload, thread_id=...)` call via BaseAgent.tools (shared_gateway). Ordering is deliberately untouched -- no PublishIntent, no confirmation wait -- because S4 was split: 'reach the Gateway' and 'wait for a human' are orthogonal, and merging them makes the 'migration does not change the contract' red line impossible to verify in isolation. S4b takes the wait. THREE pre-existing facts had to be handled first, found by recon: (1) the mainline never passed account_id at all -- the S2 defect ('account-keyed cooldown has no production writer') had TWO paths from the same XHSPublisher.publish_note, S3 closed the control-plane one, this closes the mainline one; (2) the tool hardcoded settings.platform.cdp_endpoint while the mainline resolves per account, so a straight migration would have silently sent every multi-account publish to the global browser profile -- cdp_endpoint is now a tool parameter (explicit wins, empty falls back to global so the control plane is unchanged); (3) BaseAgent.tools is a property returning shared_gateway(), which PublisherAgent previously bypassed entirely. KEY DESIGN: _publish_gateway_account_id is NOT _publish_account_id. The former returns "" when unspecified, the latter falls back to "default". The idempotency RECORD keeps "default" (compute_publish_id needs a stable string to hash; changing it would re-key every existing record and silently disarm the duplicate guard) while the PLATFORM layer gets "" (handing it "default" would file unattributed posts under account:default and change the meaning of a guardrail that works today). Two call sites, two requirements, two functions. _result_from_gateway is the single place Gateway vocabulary (ok/error_kind) is translated back into the publish_result contract (status/error), which is what keeps the 8 downstream consumers byte-unchanged (analyst/calibrator/analytics/free/workflow/hydration/omp_bridge). Two contract translations were ACCEPTED rather than patched: the timeout wording now belongs to the runtime ("timeout after 900s" replaces the method-name-carrying exception text; the test asserts the VERDICT -- status unknown + error_type publish_result_unknown -- not the wording), and the "RuntimeError: cookie expired..." prefix is harmless because classify_publish_error is a substring match, so auth_expired is unchanged. THE PINNED TRIPWIRE FIRED AND WAS RETARGETED, NOT DELETED: test_audit's 'the only orphan is the publisher' said in its own docstring that P2a wiring a publisher would fail it on purpose; it now asserts orphans == () as test_no_capability_is_left_without_an_agent, and the four-tool-users list became five. MOOT POINT WORTH RECORDING: the mutation 'the tool ignores the cdp_endpoint it is handed' SURVIVED on the first full run. Asking 'is the mutated code actually executed?' showed it is NOT -- every test replaces _get_publisher wholesale, so the factory body (and the explicit-beats-global rule) had ZERO execution coverage. A real gap, not a fake mutation: TestGetPublisherEndpointSelection now patches only XHSPublisher so the selection logic really runs, and the mutant dies. Gates: pytest 3151 passed/3 skipped (3144 + 7 = exactly the new cases: test_run_publish +4, test_xhs_publisher +3 -> zero existing cases changed apart from the intended tripwire), ruff 499 files, mypy 202 files clean, P1b baseline drift within threshold, tool_runtime_gate OK with publisher.py declared=1 invoked=1 and the orphan line GONE (named by agents: 10, orphans == ()). Mutation self-check 13/13 killed, each from original bytes by a named assertion; M1/M2/M12 (declaration/call-site capability names) are killed by the GATE first, which is the point of a compile-time rule. Stub seam: patch backend.tools.xhs.publisher._get_publisher -- browser layer only -- so the tool's normalisation, the catalog and the Gateway all really run; file runtime dropped 125.8s -> 4.3s, i.e. those tests used to touch a real browser. Open question 3 is now half-answered in code: the mainline passes its content-level publish_id AS the runtime's request-level idempotency_key (documented in-place, still no formal verdict). Open question 1 and the 501 fallback remain S4b/S5's.
